Data.title: Broadcom CEO's AI Gambling Warning Hits Chip Stocks, Samsung Falls 7%
Data.body: Key takeaways Broadcom CEO compares speculative AI investing to gambling Samsung falls 7.4% as SK Hynix loses 10% Chinese memory advances deepen pressure on semiconductor valuations Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has warned that speculative investing in artificial intelligence increasingly resembles casino gambling, adding to concerns surrounding the global AI boom as semiconductor stocks suffer another sharp selloff. Samsung Electronics shares fell approximately 7.4% on Tuesday, October 13, while rival SK Hynix plunged 10%. The losses followed a 2.7% decline in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index on Monday, extending a broader retreat in AI-related technology stocks. However, the selloff reflects more than Tan's comments, with growing competition from Chinese memory manufacturers raising fresh questions about the industry's profitability. Broadcom CEO Warns AI Investors Are Taking Casino-Like Risks Speaking during a technology panel in Singapore on October 12, Tan criticized investors who commit capital to artificial intelligence without fully understanding the companies or technologies involved. According to Reuters , Tan compared parts of the investment frenzy to casino gambling, warning that unrealistic expectations can leave investors exposed when AI companies fail to deliver anticipated returns. The Broadcom executive also identified financing as a growing challenge for the industry. While semiconductor manufacturers are gradually overcoming wafer and memory shortages, securing sufficient investment capital could become a more significant constraint on AI expansion. His remarks were not a rejection of artificial intelligence itself. Tan acknowledged that OpenAI and Anthropic have demonstrated substantial revenue-generating potential through their latest AI models. Nevertheless, questions surrounding AI revenue and infrastructure spending have increasingly influenced semiconductor valuations, particularly as companies commit billions of dollars to computing capacity. Samsung Falls 7% as Chinese Chip Competition Intensifies The latest decline was particularly severe in South Korea, where semiconductor manufacturers dominate the country's stock market. Samsung dropped 7.4%, while SK Hynix lost approximately 10%, contributing to a 5.5% decline in South Korea's KOSPI index. Japanese and European semiconductor stocks also weakened as concerns spread across global technology markets. A separate catalyst was progress announced by China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, which is developing denser DRAM architecture potentially capable of improving memory manufacturing efficiency. The development threatens to increase competition for established memory producers, including Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, although large-scale commercial production remains unproven. These concerns build on the recent Micron selloff , when investors began reassessing whether Chinese manufacturers could eventually challenge the pricing power of leading AI memory suppliers.

Data.title: BlackRock Downgrades U.S. Stocks, AI Volatility Pushes It Toward Treasuries
Data.body: Key takeaways BlackRock downgrades U.S. stocks from overweight to neutral Short-term Treasuries gain favor as yields reach 5.25% AI stocks remain attractive despite growing market volatility BlackRock has downgraded its outlook on U.S. stocks from overweight to neutral, citing heightened market volatility and increasingly attractive returns from government bonds as investors reassess the risks surrounding artificial intelligence. In its October 12 market commentary , the world's largest asset manager upgraded short-term U.S. Treasuries to overweight and longer-term Treasuries to neutral. The shift comes as 10-year Treasury yields reach approximately 5.25%, offering investors substantially higher income than in previous years. BlackRock Reduces Stock Exposure as Treasury Yields Hit 5.25% BlackRock is closing its long-held overweight position in U.S. equities to partly finance additional Treasury exposure. The firm now prefers shorter-duration government bonds, which offer income while limiting sensitivity to further interest-rate increases. The decision follows a significant change in the bond market. BlackRock had maintained an underweight position in long-term Treasuries since October 2020, when the 10-year yield stood below 0.9%. With yields now around 5.25%, government debt presents a more competitive alternative to stocks. This reversal is particularly relevant for investors who previously favored equities despite rising borrowing costs and expensive valuations. The pressure was already visible when the Nasdaq reached new highs despite Treasury yields exceeding 5.3%, highlighting how heavily market performance depended on major technology companies. AI Stock Volatility Adds Pressure to U.S. Markets Despite its downgrade, BlackRock continues to favor AI-related companies and technology infrastructure. The firm believes artificial intelligence will generate long-term economic opportunities, but higher interest rates are increasingly separating profitable businesses from those dependent on future growth expectations. That distinction matters as AI stocks face renewed selling pressure. All 30 companies in the PHLX Semiconductor Index declined during Monday's session, while Nvidia shares fell approximately 1.7%. Concerns about returns on AI infrastructure investment have also weighed on semiconductor valuations. Earlier revenue uncertainty surrounding OpenAI contributed to declines in Nvidia, AMD and other technology companies. BlackRock's decision reflects these broader risks without suggesting that the AI investment cycle has ended. What BlackRock's Downgrade Means for the S&P 500 The shift comes ahead of Wednesday's U.S. inflation report, which could influence Federal Reserve expectations and Treasury yields. Higher-than-expected inflation could increase pressure on expensive technology stocks, particularly as AI concentration leaves the S&P 500 increasingly dependent on a small group of companies.

Data.title: From “absolute control” to zero-knowledge proofs: the BIS rewrites its CBDC sales pitch
Data.body: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has published results from the second phase of Project Aurum. The second phase of Project Aurum suggests that user privacy should rely on more than the central bank’s pledge not to look. What does the Aurum prototype actually do? The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) says Project Aurum Phase 2 is an early-stage test built on its earlier Aurum code. The BIS Innovation Hub developed it with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and other institutions. It combines several privacy tools like encryption and zero-knowledge proofs, which let a payment be verified without revealing the names tied to the transaction or the amount. Under the design , people would still sign up through their regular banks. Those banks will verify their identity and keep their records, without the central bank having access to any of that information. Personal details will only be provided if the law demands it. This is a notable shift in tone from 2020, when BIS general manager Agustín Carstens said a central bank digital currency ( CBDC ) would give the issuer “absolute control on the rules and regulations” governing its use. He made the remark on an IMF panel, and conspiracy theorists later seized on it. Why should privacy be enforced? In August 2026, a European Central Bank board member, Piero Cipollone, said the planned digital euro would deliver the maximum level of privacy of any current technology, insisting the Eurosystem could not structurally link people to their transactions. Civil society groups, including an Austrian digital rights organization called Epicenter.works, wrote a joint statement , warning that legislative promises regarding the digital euro can be reinterpreted or broken. A research paper by Jeff Nijsse and Andrea Pinto looked at 20 CBDC projects and found that privacy features promised in early proposals usually get watered down by launch. However, Project Aurum is yet to be released or used commercially. The BIS report also admits that stronger privacy can make transactions slower, make programmable features harder to build, and make lost wallets difficult to recover. Data.title: Bitcoin Investor Charts How XRP Would Hit $30 XRP Price
Data.body: XRP has been quiet for a long time, but Bitcoin Boy (@btcbox123) thinks that’s about to change. The crypto analyst recently posted a long-term XRP/USD chart alongside a bold prediction. He believes XRP is heading to $30. He said, “XRP is gonna hit $30 just like this, so all we can do is wait in anticipation.” He also acknowledged the pushback he’s received, noting he has been “getting mocked nonstop.” Analyzing the Chart The chart covers over a decade of XRP price history. It runs from 2014 all the way to a projected 2027 timeline, using a logarithmic scale. Two major periods stand out. The first runs from 2014 to 2017. XRP stayed flat and uneventful before surging sharply into late 2017, reaching above $3. Many analysts still believe XRP can recreate this historic breakout . The second period is bigger. It spans 2018 to 2024. During those years, XRP was below the $1.50 to $2.10 resistance zone. This trend changed after a sharp 500% breakout in late 2024 . The chart shows that the resistance zone flipped to support after this move. XRPはこんな感じで30$行くから楽しみに待つだけ。馬鹿にされ続けてるけど、マジで30$行くから見ててくれ。 #XRP pic.twitter.com/WdkfRyqFiv — ₿₿ (@btcbox123) October 12, 2026 What the Pattern Shows Bitcoin Boy’s chart compares the two periods. A longer base, in his view, produces a larger move. The 2024 breakout was not the entire move. The chart suggests another upward move is imminent. A rising trendline connects XRP’s lows from 2020 onward. The chart narrows toward 2024 before the projected breakout begins. XRP recently tested that support while sitting in the chart’s horizontal support zone. These areas help prevent a further decline as the asset builds toward the projected move. The $30 Target From the $1.50 support level marked on the chart, a move to $30 would represent a gain of roughly 1,900%. Bitcoin Boy has not given a specific date. The chart’s projection covers a general window of 2025 to 2027. XRP tested the resistance zone near $2.10 recently and pulled back. A clean break above it would be a significant development for the trade setup Bitcoin Boy has outlined. With that zone acting as support , it could contribute significantly to the asset’s growth. Bitcoin Boy knows people doubt him. He said so himself. But his view has not changed. He sees a pattern repeating: a long consolidation followed by a major move, and he believes XRP will hit $30. Data.title: Oil Price Falls 2% Toward $105 as U.S. Turns to Russian Diesel
Data.body: Brent falls nearly 2% despite Middle East attacks U.S. temporarily authorizes transactions involving Russian diesel Analysts question Russia's 3.5-million-ton monthly export target Oil prices fell nearly 2% on Tuesday, October 13, as the United States eased sanctions on Russian diesel, raising hopes of additional fuel supplies despite continuing disruptions across the Middle East. Brent crude futures declined $2.02, or 1.89%, to $104.63 per barrel at 10:49 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 2.02% to $91.85. The retreat followed Monday's nearly $2 rally, which had pushed Brent to its highest settlement since September 15. However, the prospect of additional Russian diesel shipments may provide less relief than the market initially anticipates. U.S. Allows Russian Diesel Imports Until April 2027 On October 9, the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued General License 135 , temporarily authorizing transactions involving the sale, delivery, unloading and importation of Russian-origin diesel. The authorization runs until April 7, 2027, including imports into the United States. It does not lift all Russia-related sanctions or permit certain transactions involving restricted Russian government accounts. The decision followed President Donald Trump's announcement of an agreement intended to increase Russian diesel supplies to international markets. Moscow has suggested exports could reach 3–3.5 million metric tons monthly by year-end, but the figure represents a target rather than confirmed deliveries. According to Reuters, PVM Oil Associates analyst Tamas Varga questioned whether Russia could meet that target given damage to its refining infrastructure. The proposed volumes also face transportation, financing and logistical challenges. Why Brent Remains Above $100 Despite New Supply Hopes The decline comes as energy traders balance potential Russian exports against continuing supply disruptions around the Persian Gulf. Recent attacks on Saudi infrastructure and commercial vessels have renewed concerns about regional oil transportation, while insurance and freight expenses remain elevated. Coinpaper previously reported that physical crude delivered to Asia can cost substantially more than benchmark futures prices because of shipping risks and regional supply premiums. The Russian agreement addresses refined diesel availability rather than directly adding equivalent quantities of crude oil production. That distinction matters because the global market faces separate shortages of raw petroleum, refinery capacity and finished fuels. Earlier this month, Gulf oil exports recovered substantially, yet diesel supply constraints persisted. Can Russian Diesel Actually Lower Global Oil Prices? The U.S. policy shift comes as energy markets remain sensitive to relatively small changes in available supply. OPEC recently reduced its 2026 oil demand growth forecast , but weak demand growth has not eliminated physical-market shortages. Russia's additional diesel could ease regional fuel tightness if shipments materialize, although analysts question whether damaged refineries can sustain the proposed export volumes.

Data.title: Ledger: LTE Implants in CryptoBilis Wallets Stole Seed Phrases
Data.body: BitcoinWorld Ledger: LTE Implants in CryptoBilis Wallets Stole Seed Phrases Ledger says unauthorized implants hidden inside hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis quietly captured users’ 24-word recovery phrases and shipped them out over cellular networks, a finding that has triggered a reseller shutdown and pulled two rival manufacturers out of their distribution agreements. The disclosure came via a Tuesday post on X from Ledger Donjon, the company’s security research team, and was reported by Cointelegraph . Ledger says the implant sat inside the wallet casing, read the seed phrase off the screen during initial setup, and exfiltrated it via LTE using an embedded eSIM. The component did not touch the secure chip, the system software, or transaction signing, and confirmed losses so far trace back to devices sold through CryptoBilis. The technical picture, as Ledger describes it, is narrow but effective: a microcontroller decodes the recovery phrase at the moment a new wallet displays it for backup, then a cellular module with its own eSIM pushes the words off the device — no tampering with the signing path required. Ledger says it has sold more than 8 million hardware wallets, devices built to keep private keys offline and confirm transactions on-screen. CryptoBilis was listed as an authorized reseller in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. The problem surfaced publicly on Oct. 9, when crypto losses tied to Ledger devices bought through the reseller began circulating. Ledger confirmed on Oct. 10 that one affected user’s device contained an unauthorized component, according to PANews . Key facts Ledger Donjon identified an implant that decodes the on-screen 24-word recovery phrase and transmits it over LTE through an embedded SIM, per Cointelegraph. Ledger confirmed the implant in one user’s device on Oct. 10; the related losses were first disclosed publicly on Oct. 9, PANews reported. Third-party loss estimates diverge — Specter put the figure above $86 million and Yfarmx raised its own to $103 million — and Ledger has not confirmed any total. CryptoBilis suspended sales and shipments of all hardware wallet brands across Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia, and closed its physical stores temporarily. Trezor removed CryptoBilis from its authorized reseller network, and OneKey terminated the reseller agreement while offering free replacements for devices bought from CryptoBilis between March 1 and Oct. 12, 2026, with applications open through Dec. 31. The two accounts agree on the mechanism, not the money Cointelegraph lays out the device-level details — the microcontroller, the eSIM, the LTE channel — and stresses that neither the security chip nor transaction approval was modified. PANews’ write-up of the same Ledger post matches that description almost point for point, adding that the component sits inside the casing and that the total number of affected users remains unverified. Where the two reports part ways is the damage estimate. Cointelegraph cites Specter’s figure of more than $86 million and Yfarmx’s revised estimate of $103 million, while noting that Ledger has not confirmed a total; PANews states that all confirmed fund losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis without endorsing a dollar amount. The gap between the two third-party estimates is itself the clearest signal that the number is still being assembled. The incident may not be limited to one distributor. Ledger says it is reviewing reports that fall outside CryptoBilis, and PANews reports the same widening scope, describing an investigation into similar implant reports involving other resellers and regions. Cointelegraph adds a concrete example: an X user named Johannes said he bought two Ledger devices from separate MediaMarkt stores in Europe and found implants in both. Ledger has not confirmed whether those European devices connect to the CryptoBilis batch. Why it matters Self-custody relies on a single premise — that the recovery phrase never leaves the device except when the owner writes it down. This implant does not break cryptography; it attacks the moment of display, which means a compromised unit can look and behave exactly like a genuine one until the seed has already been sent. That is a harder problem to spot than a firmware flaw, because nothing in the wallet’s normal operation signals anything wrong. The fallout is also hitting the distribution layer, not just the manufacturer. Two competing wallet brands cut CryptoBilis off even after saying they had found no evidence their own products were affected — a sign that resellers, not just devices, are now part of the trust calculation for buyers. CryptoBilis has said it is reviewing its processes with independent specialists. Ledger is directing anyone who suspects tampering to contact its support team, file a police report, and consult an inspection guide. That guide carries a practical warning: opening a device can damage it, so users are told to back up their recovery phrases first. What to watch Two open threads will shape the next phase. Ledger has yet to publish a verified count of affected users or a total loss figure, and it is still investigating whether implants appeared through resellers other than CryptoBilis. On the reseller side, OneKey’s replacement window for devices bought from CryptoBilis between March 1 and Oct. 12 runs through Dec. 31, giving affected buyers a firm deadline to act. Frequently Asked Questions What exactly did the implant in the CryptoBilis wallets do? According to Ledger, the component sat inside the device casing, read what appeared on the screen, decoded the 24-word recovery phrase shown during initial setup, and sent it out over LTE using a built-in eSIM. Did the implant break the wallet’s security chip? No. Both Ledger and PANews’ account of the company’s post say the component did not alter the secure chip, the wallet system, or the transaction signing process. Which companies stopped working with CryptoBilis? Trezor removed CryptoBilis from its authorized reseller network and OneKey terminated the reseller’s authorization, according to Cointelegraph. CryptoBilis also suspended sales and shipments of all hardware wallet brands across three Southeast Asian markets. How large were the losses from the incident? Estimates from third parties differ: blockchain investigator Specter put potential losses above $86 million and Yfarmx raised its own estimate to $103 million, but Ledger has not confirmed a total. Were any wallets sold outside CryptoBilis affected? Ledger is examining reports beyond that reseller, and an X user named Johannes said he found implants in two Ledger devices bought from separate MediaMarkt stores in Europe. Ledger has not confirmed a link between the European reports and the CryptoBilis batch. This post Ledger: LTE Implants in CryptoBilis Wallets Stole Seed Phrases first appeared on BitcoinWorld .

Data.title: XRP’s 100 Billion Supply Cap Is Safe After RippleX Fixes a Critical XRPL Flaw
Data.body: RippleX, Ripple’s engineering and software development team, has patched a critical vulnerability in the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Notably, the flaw could have let attackers create about 18.45 trillion XRP in a single transaction, potentially breaching the network’s original 100 billion token supply cap. Researchers from US-based cybersecurity startup Veria Labs discovered the flaw using an artificial intelligence-powered security agent, which developed a working exploit in a local test environment. The vulnerability had remained undetected in the XRPL’s payment-processing code since 2015. In an October 12 report, the researchers warned that the flaw could have put XRP’s reported $94 billion market value at risk. The vulnerability involved an integer overflow in XRPL’s payment engine. When a transaction processed multiple decentralized exchange orders, the software could incorrectly calculate the total XRP required to settle them. This allowed sellers to receive the full amounts associated with their orders while the buyer was charged substantially less. A second arithmetic error in the ledger’s supply-protection mechanism could then prevent the transaction from being rejected. Veria Labs estimated that a single successful transaction could create more than 184 times XRPL’s original XRP supply. The researchers also said the attack could be repeated under the right conditions. “An attacker could have created spendable XRP far beyond the total supply in a single validated transaction,” Veria Labs stated. The firm reported the vulnerability on September 22, 2026. The fix was merged the following day, and the emergency software release, rippled 3.4.1, arrived on September 25. The response bypassed XRPL’s standard amendment process, which generally requires support from more than 80% of trusted validators over two weeks. For context, developers opted for an immediate software update because publishing the patch while waiting for the usual approval process could have exposed the vulnerability to attackers before the network was fully protected. The disclosure says more than 80% of default validators upgraded on release day. The disclosure follows a separate August security incident in which an attacker stole approximately $200,000 from the tx XRPL cross-chain bridge. The attack involved software that incorrectly recognized transactions as deposits even though the corresponding XRP had not reached the bridge’s reserves. The bridge operator subsequently halted the service and addressed the vulnerability. That said, on Sunday XRPL developers announced plans to strengthen security testing through mandatory retesting of fixed vulnerabilities before releases and expanded AI-assisted bug detection. “Together with RippleX and the community, we will ensure the XRP Ledger is protected against such vulnerabilities. This means radically applying Formal Verification and AI adversarial testing, collaborating closely with security researchers, and strengthening the bug bounty program.” They stated on X.

Data.title: Whale's Insight: What Can Bitcoin Add To Your Stock Portfolio?
Data.body: Summary Bitcoin still fails the hedge test. In 3 of 4 major equity stress episodes since 2020, Bitcoin fell materially more than stocks. Its correlation with equities is also unstable, shifting between positive, near-zero and negative territory across market regimes. But even a small allocation has historically made a difference. In Fidelity’s 2016–2025 backtest, adding just 1% Bitcoin to a traditional 60/40 portfolio lifted annual returns from 9.44% to 11.25%, while volatility rose only slightly from 10.26% to 10.65%. Crypto’s portfolio value goes beyond hedging. Its 24/7 market can provide an early read on risk appetite, its higher volatility can add return potential, and large moves can create rebalancing opportunities. That makes crypto a conditional diversifier, not portfolio insurance. Could a small Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) allocation actually improve a traditional portfolio? In a 10-year Fidelity backtest, adding just 1% BTC lifted annual returns from 9.44% to 11.25%, with volatility rising only slightly. But Bitcoin still fails a key hedge test when stocks sell off. So, what does crypto really add to a portfolio? Bitcoin still fails the hedge test. In 3 of 4 major equity stress episodes since 2020, Bitcoin fell materially more than stocks. Its correlation with equities is also unstable, shifting between positive, near-zero and negative territory across market regimes. But even a small allocation has historically made a difference. In Fidelity's 2016-2025 backtest, adding just 1% Bitcoin to a traditional 60/40 portfolio lifted annual returns from 9.44% to 11.25%, while volatility rose only slightly from 10.26% to 10.65%. Crypto's portfolio value goes beyond hedging. Its 24/7 market can provide an early read on risk appetite, its higher volatility can add return potential, and large moves can create rebalancing opportunities. That makes crypto a conditional diversifier, not portfolio insurance. Bitcoin is pulling away from stocks again. Its 260-day correlation with the S&P 500 has fallen to its lowest level since 2015, as crypto increasingly trades on its own drivers. That raises a portfolio question: if Bitcoin is moving more independently from equities, what can it actually add to a stock portfolio? It depends on the role Bitcoin is expected to play. Diversification and hedging serve different purposes. A diversifier only needs to behave differently enough to improve the portfolio. A hedge faces a tougher test: it needs to provide protection when stocks actually fall. And by that standard, Bitcoin's record looks very different. Why Crypto Is Not a Reliable Equity Hedge History gives a fairly clear answer. When risk-off hits, crypto usually falls with stocks, only harder. In 3 of the 4 major stress episodes above, Bitcoin fell materially more than the equity indices. In the fourth, it roughly matched them. None offered meaningful downside protection, and in most cases, a Bitcoin allocation would have added to portfolio volatility at exactly the wrong moment. More importantly, a reliable hedge should provide downside protection when equities fall. Bitcoin's relationship with stocks has instead moved between positive, near-zero and even negative territory, only to turn strongly positive again during some periods of market stress. March 2026 made that unusually clear. As the Iran conflict hit global risk assets, Bitcoin's 30-day correlation with the S&P 500 jumped to 0.74, the highest level of the year, even as its longer-term correlation continued to trend lower. Why does this happen? Shared liquidity exposure. Higher rates tighten financial conditions and drain liquidity, putting pressure on assets that depend heavily on risk appetite. Similar sensitivity to risk-off moves. High-beta tech and crypto both sit toward the riskier end of the market, so investors tend to cut exposure to both when risk appetite deteriorates. Crypto-specific drivers matter, until macro takes over. ETF flows, stablecoin liquidity, leverage and regulation can drive Bitcoin independently for months. But during a macro shock, those factors can quickly become secondary. Bitcoin's correlation with equities changes considerably across market conditions, making it difficult to rely on during periods of stress. Its diversification benefits remain conditional, particularly when broader liquidity pressures affect both markets. What Can Crypto Add to a Portfolio Hedging is only one possible role. Crypto's broader portfolio value can come from three different places. First, crypto can provide an early read on risk appetite. Crypto trades around the clock, so it can reveal changes in market sentiment while equity markets are closed. A sharp weekend move in Bitcoin, for example, can offer an early read on the risk environment before stocks reopen on Monday. The signal becomes more meaningful when price, funding rates and open interest move in the same direction. One caveat: crypto has its own shocks. An exchange failure, forced liquidation or other crypto-specific event may say little about stocks. These signals can be useful, but they don't always carry over to equities. Second, crypto can add higher return potential. Stocks already range from defensive names to high-growth tech. Crypto can sit even further out on that spectrum: more volatile, but with potentially greater upside. Historical portfolio tests show how even a small allocation can matter. In Fidelity's 2016-2025 backtest, adding 1% Bitcoin to a traditional 60/40 portfolio lifted annual returns from 9.44% to 11.25%, while annual volatility rose only slightly, from 10.26% to 10.65%. These historical results don't guarantee future returns or imply that Bitcoin makes a portfolio safer. Still, a small allocation can introduce another source of potential returns. Third, crypto's volatility can create rebalancing opportunities. Because crypto can move much faster than the rest of a portfolio, its weight can quickly drift away from its original target. After a strong rally, rebalancing can trim that exposure; after a large decline, it can restore it. Rebalancing helps investors maintain their target allocation as crypto prices fluctuate, without requiring them to predict short-term market moves. That still depends on the long-term case for the asset remaining intact; otherwise, adding after a decline is simply averaging down. So crypto does not need to hedge equities to have a role alongside them. It can provide information, add return potential, and create opportunities to rebalance. What Role Does Crypto Actually Play Crypto remains an unreliable equity hedge, and its diversification benefits depend on market conditions. Its value lies more in the market information, return potential and portfolio exposure it can provide. That role is not fixed. Bitcoin's investor base is changing, institutional ownership is growing, and its relationship with traditional markets may change with it. The real test will come during future periods of equity stress. If Bitcoin increasingly holds its ground while stocks sell off, the case for treating it as a hedge will become stronger. For now, crypto is best viewed as a separate portfolio exposure, with its own risks and opportunities. Data.title: Concerns About Selling Pressure on Bitcoin Are Growing: What Do the US Transfers Mean? Analysis Company Explains!
Data.body: Recently, after a long period of silence, there was increased activity in wallets linked to the US government, with billions of dollars worth of Bitcoin being transferred. At this point, the transfer of approximately $1.54 billion worth of Bitcoin and Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) from US government-affiliated wallets to Coinbase Prime has raised concerns about a sell-off in the cryptocurrency market. US Government’s $1.54 Billion Bitcoin Transfer: Sale or Custody Move? However, according to an analysis by the analytics company K33 Research, the majority of these transfers are considered to be for safekeeping and asset management purposes rather than sales. According to on-chain data, approximately 17,733 BTC and 750 WBTC were transferred in recent days. The total value of the Bitcoins is estimated at approximately $1.48 billion, while the WBTC is valued at $62 million, bringing the total transaction volume to $1.54 billion. K33 Research also stated that when other wallets considered to be linked to the government are taken into account, the amount of Bitcoin reaching Coinbase Prime could rise to approximately 21,500 BTC. While no official statement has been made regarding the transfers, K33 Research reported that they believe the majority of the transferred BTC were not sold. “Coinbase Prime has been operating the US Police Department’s digital asset custody service since 2024. Therefore, it is highly likely that this transfer was made for asset custody purposes rather than a sale. Furthermore, considering transactions from unidentified wallets, we estimate the total transfer volume may have reached approximately 21,500 BTC.” K33 Research stated that transfers alone are not sufficient to conclude that they will create strong selling pressure on the Bitcoin price, adding that the real determining factor for the market will be whether the transferred assets are actually put up for sale. The company also noted that a significant portion of the transfers consisted of 12,267 BTC linked to the 2016 attack on the Bitfinex cryptocurrency exchange. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Ledger reveals how hidden chip stole recovery phrases in $93M hack
Data.body: Ledger revealed that a secret chip embedded in hardware wallets from its reseller CryptoBilis captured 24-word recovery phrases from the screen and transmitted them via the cellular network to the attacker, which researchers estimated to cost between $84.2 million and $93.2 million. The French firm revealed the details of the attack vector for the first time in a blog post update on X on Tuesday made by its security team, Ledger Donjon. This is perhaps the most detailed explanation of how the owners of the compromised devices lost access to their cryptocurrency without even touching Ledger’s software. How the implant pulled keys off the screen The additional chip was located inside the device’s housing, according to Ledger. While setting up the wallet, when the user shows the 24 words that serve as a backup for the account, the microcontroller of the implant reads them and translates them into data that is transmitted over LTE via an integrated SIM card. Such a recovery code is basically an account. With its help, you can restore your wallet on another piece of hardware without having to use the compromised device and perform any transactions. Update on Ledger devices at MediaMarkt Saturn 🔽 As of Oct. 13th, MediaMarkt Saturn has stopped, with Ledger’s alignment, the sale of Ledger devices in their stores and online while the investigation continues, following the report of an implant from one customer in Germany. No loss of funds were reported. We have no indication that Ledger’s infrastructure, systems or services were compromised. Ledger Support is reviewing user reports, and Ledger’s cybersecurity experts, the Donjon will be examining the devices we receive: https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq. If you have questions about a device you bought, contact Ledger Support at https://t.co/QzukOZdEzq. Ledger will never call you, message you directly or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. Many claims and figures circulating online are unverified. Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger and MediaMarkt Saturn channels for updates. We will share more as the investigation continues. — Ledger (@Ledger) October 13, 2026 According to reports, the hacked devices were the Ledger Nano X model. Mark Karpelès, former CEO of Mt. Gox and now at Karpeles Lab, shared a picture of the implant hidden behind the screen and noted that the antenna cable of the latter was the clue. The research laboratory Tibane Labs confirmed the discovery and said it had two versions of the implant, including one with an ST STM32G431KBU6 microcontroller, a 2×2 mm eSIM, and an LTE module. A supply-chain attack, not a software breach However, Ledger made sure to outline what was spared by the attack . The implant didn’t harm the Secure Element, the chip that ensures the safety of private keys. It didn’t affect the operating system, and it had no impact on transactions and signatures, as stated by the company in its X post. The company characterized the incident as a physical attack on its supply chain and not a hacking incident against its software or internal processes. Ledger, the company claims that it ships more than 8 million devices, pointed out that its “Genuine Check” system is unable to detect any implant while the original Secure Element remains untouched. Ledger theft estimates top $86M as Tether blocks $10M Ledger has not released any data on the number of victims or the value involved. However, on-chain research firms have done their work and arrived at their numbers. Reports say that about $93.2 million in losses are spread through more than 300 wallets. But investigator Specter puts the losses beyond $86 million, and Yfarmx increases its figure to $103 million. Tether is freezing $10 million worth of its USDT stablecoin associated with the theft. This was discovered on October 9 when Ledger started an investigation into the alleged funds draining and asked CryptoBilis to stop selling its signers. Ledger revealed on October 10 that one of the compromised users’ devices contained an illegal implant. So far, all of the losses confirmed involve a unit sold by CryptoBilis, an authorized reseller in Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines. Rivals cut ties with CryptoBilis CryptoBilis reportedly stopped all of its sales and deliveries of hardware wallets of different brands in the three countries and closed down its brick-and-mortar stores, expanding on an earlier move that involved the Ledger brand alone. The reseller company stated that it was reviewing the situation with the help of outside experts. Trezor stated that it did not see any evidence of tampering with its devices resold by CryptoBilis, yet decided to remove the reseller from its list of authorized distributors. OneKey company stated that there were no losses reported to be associated with this case and also removed CryptoBilis from its list of authorized resellers; additionally, it offered free replacement for OneKey devices purchased via CryptoBilis between March 1 and October 12, 2026. Reports beyond the reseller “Ledger said it is investigating reports of implants in devices not sold by CryptoBilis, but it has not confirmed yet a theft in a device purchased from any other store,” reported Cointelegraph. In addition, according to Cointelegraph, there was an X user named Johannes who uploaded pictures of two Ledger devices which he claims were purchased separately from MediaMarkt stores in Europe and both were implanted. Ledger has not yet confirmed any connection between the reports in Europe and the CryptoBilis case. The advice for the users of CryptoBilis products, according to Ledger, is very clear: do not initialize a signer from CryptoBilis and if you have initialized one, then move funds to another device with a new recovery phrase. Data.title: XRP’s $1 Lifeline Could Unlock $10 and $20 Targets as XRPL Patches Decade-Old Flaw That Risked Billions in Fake XRP
Data.body: XRP has climbed 70% from its previous accumulation zone, according to market analyst Crypto Patel, who says the $1 to $1.20 range is critical to the top altcoin’s next major move. Source: Crypto Patel Presently trading at $1.37 per CoinGecko data , XRP is well above the accumulation zone between $0.75 and $0.95 identified by Crypto Patel. Notably, the analyst has identified the $1 to $1.20 zone as a potential re-entry zone, depending on whether XRP can hold support around the psychologically important $1 level. If bulls successfully defend this threshold, the cryptocurrency could resume its upward trajectory, with long-term targets of $10 and $20. Nevertheless, if XRP loses the $1 support level, Crypto Patel expects a wait-and-see approach to take center stage, as a potential return to the earlier accumulation zone could trigger instead of chasing the price lower. As price action continues to play out in the XRP market, whales are watching from the sidelines , contemplating the next move, as reported by ZyCrypto. Decade-Old XRP Ledger Vulnerability Raises Security Questions The XRP Ledger is drawing notable attention after researchers discovered a serious security vulnerability dating back to 2015. At the nick of time, researchers demonstrated a flaw that could have let attackers create and spend XRP without properly funding it, threatening the network’s fixed supply of 100 billion tokens. Reports indicated the exploit could have enabled the creation of as much as 18 trillion XRP. An emergency software fix was released on September 25 after researchers demonstrated the exploit, and Ripple said there was no evidence the vulnerability had been exploited on public networks. Therefore, the disclosure underscores the importance of ongoing security reviews as blockchain networks evolve.

Data.title: Goldman Sachs, Citadel and Google Alumni Bring RWA Perpetuals On-Chain with DeepSigma
Data.body: DeepSigma has launched a live paper-trading demo covering 77 real-world markets, using Cypherium's patented blockchain technology to bring decentralized perpetual trading beyond crypto. A team of former Goldman Sachs, Citadel Securities, Google and Uber professionals is bringing perpetual futures trading to traditional financial markets with the launch of DeepSigma, a decentralized exchange focused on real-world assets (RWAs). Unveiled on October 13, the platform currently offers a live paper-trading demo spanning 77 markets, including U.S. equities, major stock indexes, commodities, sector ETFs and Treasury yields. The exchange is powered by Cypherium, a Layer 1 blockchain backed by four granted U.S. patents, and aims to address some of the challenges that have made bringing traditional financial derivatives on-chain more complicated than their crypto counterparts. Unlike tokenized asset platforms, DeepSigma does not require traders to own or take custody of the underlying assets. Instead, its perpetual contracts track real-world market prices through external data sources, allowing users to take long or short positions without owning the assets themselves. Bringing Crypto-Style Perpetuals to Traditional Markets Perpetual futures have become a major part of crypto trading, but applying the same model to traditional assets presents a different set of technical and market-structure challenges. While cryptocurrencies trade around the clock, traditional financial markets operate within defined trading hours. Liquidity can also vary significantly, and price discovery becomes more complicated when underlying markets are closed. DeepSigma is developing its infrastructure specifically around these differences. Its risk-management framework includes multi-source pricing, mark-price mechanisms, position and exposure limits, circuit breakers, partial liquidations and an insurance mechanism designed for stressed market conditions. The platform also uses a central limit order book alongside a clearing layer responsible for managing positions, collateral, margin and settlement. "Crypto has already demonstrated the demand for perpetual markets, but you cannot simply take the same model and put a stock or commodity ticker on it," said Sky Guo, CEO of DeepSigma and founder of Cypherium. "Real-world markets have different trading hours, liquidity conditions, pricing sources and regulatory considerations. We started DeepSigma with those differences in mind." The current demo includes perpetual markets tracking major indexes such as the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, Dow Jones Industrial Average, Russell 2000 and VIX. It also covers commodities including gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas and copper, alongside U.S. Treasury yields. Beyond paper trading, DeepSigma's terminal integrates market data, technical indicators, asset-specific news, portfolio tracking and a competitive leaderboard. An AI Market Analysis Desk can also generate potential trading strategies, although the system operates entirely off-chain and cannot execute trades or move user assets. Patented Cypherium Blockchain Powers the Exchange A central component of DeepSigma's infrastructure is Cypherium, the open, permissionless Layer 1 blockchain also founded by Guo. Cypherium combines Proof-of-Work with HotStuff-derived Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus, an architecture designed to support high-throughput blockchain applications. The technology is covered by four granted U.S. patents, numbered 12,443,569, 11,907,174, 11,516,006 and 11,411,721, covering blockchain consensus and related technology. According to the project, Cypherium is designed to process hundreds of thousands of transactions per second, providing the underlying infrastructure for high-frequency financial activity. Guo, who is also a named inventor on Cypherium's patents, previously co-authored DLT Options for CBDC with Thomas Moser of the Swiss National Bank and has spoken at the United Nations Headquarters and Nasdaq. Wall Street and Big Tech Experience Behind DeepSigma DeepSigma's leadership combines experience from traditional finance, quantitative trading and technology. The team includes Albert Xu, the company's CFO and a former FICC portfolio manager at Goldman Sachs, and Jenny Chen, its Chief Quant Director, who previously worked at Citadel Securities and was recognized as a Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance honoree. Chaoran Wang, DeepSigma's CTO, previously worked as an engineer at Google and Uber and founded quantitative trading firm UmiUmi. The combination of financial-market and blockchain expertise reflects DeepSigma's approach to building derivatives infrastructure for assets that operate differently from cryptocurrencies. "The hardest part of bringing real-world assets on-chain isn't creating another market symbol. It's making sure the market still behaves sensibly when the underlying asset is closed, liquidity disappears or an external price moves sharply," Guo explained. Privacy and Regulatory Readiness Built Into the Design DeepSigma is also developing decentralized identity infrastructure intended to support regulatory eligibility requirements without exposing unnecessary personal information on-chain. The proposed system follows a "prove eligibility, not identity" approach, using zero-knowledge proofs to allow participants to demonstrate that they meet certain requirements without publishing their underlying personal data. The company says it has designed the platform around U.S. regulatory frameworks from the outset and is working with specialized digital-asset counsel. Rather than treating compliance as something to address after expansion, DeepSigma views regulatory readiness as part of its market-entry strategy. For now, the platform's publicly unveiled functionality centers on its live paper-trading demo across 77 RWA markets. DeepSigma's broader objective is to bring the perpetual futures model beyond crypto while accounting for the pricing, liquidity, risk management and regulatory requirements of traditional financial markets. Data.title: KuCoin Nigeria Receives Conditional Approval-in-Principle for Admission into SEC Nigeria’s Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme
Data.body: BitcoinWorld KuCoin Nigeria Receives Conditional Approval-in-Principle for Admission into SEC Nigeria’s Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme OYO STATE, Nigeria, Oct. 13, 2026 /CNW/ — KuCoin Nigeria Limited has received conditional Approval-in-Principle (AIP) from the Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria (SEC Nigeria), for admission into its Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme (ARIP). The development marks another important milestone in KuCoin’s global regulatory journey and further reflects the company’s long-term commitment to strengthening its global compliance framework and building trusted digital asset infrastructure. As part of the AIP review process, KuCoin Nigeria demonstrated elements of its proposed platform and operating model to SEC Nigeria. The demonstration covered proposed products and services for Nigeria, customer onboarding procedures, fiat on- and off-ramp arrangements, technology infrastructure, and governance and risk management structures. The conditional Approval-in-Principle is not a final registration, licence, endorsement or recommendation by SEC Nigeria and does not authorise KuCoin Nigeria to commence operations, onboard clients or offer services to the Nigerian public. However, this preparatory work reflects KuCoin’s focus on incorporating local accountability, user protection and risk management into its proposed operations. Nigeria has a vibrant digital economy and a rapidly developing digital asset ecosystem, making it one of the world’s key markets for digital asset adoption and innovation. KuCoin believes that building a healthy and sustainable digital asset market requires constructive engagement between industry participants and regulators, together with continued improvements in governance, transparency, market integrity and user protection. KuCoin’s regulatory engagement in Nigeria forms part of its broader approach to meeting local requirements across key markets. In Europe, KuCoin EU has received authorisation under MiCAR, enabling it to provide regulated crypto-asset services across the European Union. In Australia, KuCoin operates through Axis One Markets Pty Ltd, which is registered with AUSTRAC as a digital currency exchange provider. Each authorisation or registration applies solely to the relevant entity and activities within the applicable jurisdiction. None of these authorisations or registrations authorises KuCoin Nigeria to operate or provide services in Nigeria. KuCoin is committed to respecting local regulatory frameworks in each market, aligning its operations with applicable requirements and obtaining the relevant authorisations or registrations in each jurisdiction. BC Wong, CEO of KuCoin, said: “Receiving conditional Approval-in-Principle from SEC Nigeria marks another important milestone in KuCoin’s global compliance journey. As digital assets become an increasingly important part of the global financial system, trust must be built through continuously strengthening governance, maintaining high compliance standards and enhancing user protection. We value the opportunity to engage constructively with SEC Nigeria through ARIP and to continue building in line with Nigeria’s evolving regulatory framework. Our focus remains on strong governance, high compliance standards and meaningful user protection as we support the responsible and sustainable development of the digital asset ecosystem.” For KuCoin, compliance is not only about meeting regulatory requirements; it is also about building long-term trust. Looking ahead, KuCoin will continue advancing responsible innovation, strengthening its global governance, operational resilience and user protection capabilities, and working with regulators, partners and industry participants to support the development of a more mature, transparent and trusted digital asset market. About KuCoin Founded in 2017, KuCoin is a leading global crypto platform built on trust and security, serving over 45 million users across 200+ countries and regions. Known for its reliability and user-first approach, the platform builds trust into every layer of the user experience, combining advanced technology, deep liquidity, and strong security safeguards to deliver a seamless trading experience. KuCoin provides access to 1,000+ digital assets through a broad product suite and remains committed to building a compliant and user-centric ecosystem for the future of finance, backed by SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, ISO 22301:2019 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certifications. The products, digital assets and services offered by KuCoin globally are not offered through KuCoin Nigeria and will not be available in Nigeria unless separately reviewed and, where required, cleared in writing by SEC Nigeria. Disclosure The conditional Approval-in-Principle granted to KuCoin Nigeria Limited relates solely to its conditional admission into SEC Nigeria’s ARIP and forms part of an ongoing regulatory review. It is not a final registration, licence, endorsement, recommendation or authorisation to commence operations and should not be interpreted as SEC Nigeria’s endorsement, recognition, recommendation or approval of any of KuCoin’s products or services. Until all applicable pre-commencement conditions have been satisfied and any further written clearance required by SEC Nigeria has been obtained, KuCoin Nigeria will not commence operations, onboard clients, list digital assets, enable trading or peer-to-peer services, process fiat on- or off-ramp transactions, hold client assets or launch public-facing services in Nigeria. Proposed products, digital assets, trading pairs, custody and wallet structures, fiat gateway arrangements, order-book-sharing arrangements and related public communications remain subject to further review and written no-objection by SEC Nigeria. KuCoin Nigeria Limited’s participation in ARIP, and any activities undertaken under the programme, remain within the scope specified by SEC Nigeria and subject to its conditions and ongoing compliance with applicable regulatory, operational and supervisory obligations. Any proposed product, service, digital asset or operational arrangement in Nigeria remains subject to applicable Nigerian regulatory requirements and, where required, further SEC Nigeria review and written no-objection. Admission into ARIP does not assure or predetermine the grant of formal registration. KuCoin remains solely responsible for the accuracy of the claims relating to its global products, operations, foreign regulatory status and certifications contained in this release.
